findings.observation: The two consequential decision trays are mounted as visual overlays, but the code does not give them modal semantics or any programmatic focus handoff.
evidence: Freeze v4 still marks matching rendered proof as missing, so no direct keyboard or assistive-technology replay is available.
src/Prototype.tsx:365-380 mounts FactDecisionTray and EffectApprovalTray as sibling overlays when stage changes.
src/Prototype.tsx:653-713 renders each tray as <motion.section> with aria-labelledby only; there is no role="dialog", aria-modal, autoFocus, or mount-time focus transfer.
findings.user_impact: Keyboard, switch, and screen-reader users have no code-evidenced guarantee that focus lands in the active decision gate instead of staying on background controls, which makes the critical fact-confirmation and effect-approval steps less reliable.
findings.recommendation: Treat each decision tray as the active task surface: add modal semantics, move focus into the tray on open, and restore focus to the invoking control on close.
findings.verification: At 393x852 with Full Keyboard Access and screen-reader navigation, opening each tray should move focus to its title or first actionable control, keep background controls out of the active sequence, and restore focus to the opener when dismissed.

findings.observation: The ambiguous-identity chooser uses custom buttons with radio roles, but the code does not implement the full keyboard radio-group pattern.
evidence: src/Prototype.tsx:793-799 renders two <button> elements with role="radio" and aria-checked state.
Those controls do not define roving tabindex, native radio inputs, or arrow-key handlers anywhere in Prototype.tsx.
findings.user_impact: Users relying on keyboard or switch-style navigation may need to tab through each option individually and may not get the expected single-tab-stop radio behavior for this conflict-resolution path.
findings.recommendation: Replace the custom pattern with native radio inputs or implement a roving-tabindex radio group with arrow-key selection and a single logical group stop.
findings.verification: With keyboard-only navigation, Tab should enter the group once, arrow keys should change the selected owner, and assistive technology should announce the newly checked option without requiring separate tab stops for every choice.

findings.observation: Some tappable controls remain below the 44 pt baseline, including the Today segmented navigation and the AX5 secondary shortcut.
evidence: By contrast, the consequential controls do declare 44 px minimums, including .source-heading-toggle at src/prototype.css:232-235 and .primary-button/.secondary-button/.text-button at src/prototype.css:315.
findings.user_impact: Touch users, especially at larger text sizes, get less forgiving targets on adjacent navigation and shortcuts, which raises miss-tap risk and weakens the mobile accessibility baseline even if the main decision controls are larger.
findings.recommendation: Raise all tappable navigation and shortcut controls to at least 44x44 pt, including the Today tabs and the AX5 secondary shortcut.
findings.verification: A fresh 393x852 render and touch-target audit should show every tappable control at or above 44x44 pt with adequate separation.

strengths: Reduced-motion handling is wired through the main screen transition, both decision trays, the executing spinner, and the global prefers-reduced-motion override in src/Prototype.tsx:321-325, src/Prototype.tsx:653-655, src/Prototype.tsx:691-693, and src/prototype.css:401-403 plus 550-552.

The main consequential controls do meet the 44 px baseline in code, including the back affordances, source toggle, and primary/secondary/text action buttons in src/prototype.css:68, src/prototype.css:74, src/prototype.css:232-235, and src/prototype.css:315.
